prompt: What is the median of the data set $3$, $7$, $1$, $9$, $5$?
hint: The median is the middle value, but only once the data are in order. Is this list in order yet?

hints.text: The median is the middle value, but only once the data are in order. Is this list in order yet?
Arrange the values from least to greatest: $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$. With five values, the median is the third one in the list.
The third value in the sorted list is $5$, so the median is $5$.

learningObjective: Find the median of an unsorted data set.
explanation: Put the values in order from least to greatest: $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$.
There are five values, so the middle one is the third, with two values on each side.
The third value is $5$, so the median of the data set is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sorting is not optional
steps: Taking the middle of the unsorted list gives $1$ — the most common error on median questions.
The median is defined by *position after sorting*, not by position as listed.
Write the sorted list on scratch paper; do not try to sort in your head.
